extracted.intended_audience: registered patent and trademark practitioners (attorneys) who use or sponsor USPTO.gov accounts
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, responsibilities, and disciplinary standards for attorneys who create, verify, or sponsor USPTO.gov accounts for trademark practice support staff, including required certifications, supervision obligations, monitoring, and sanctions for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with USPTO.gov Terms of Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a USPTO.gov account requires compliance with the Terms of Use for USPTO Websites; each time an account holder logs in they are presented with a message stating that, by signing in, they certify to the Terms of Use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account login presents an on-screen certification; attorneys and sponsored users must abide by the Terms of Use available at www.uspto.gov/terms-use-uspto-websites. Failure to comply may form the basis for disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity verification required to file electronic trademark forms
rubrics_metrics.description: As of August 6, 2022, trademark owners and attorneys were required to verify their identity to file electronic trademark forms from their then-verified USPTO.gov account; initially sponsored support staff were not required to verify identity but rules changed later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO later extended identity verification requirements for attorney-sponsored accounts (see Federal Register notices cited). Attorneys must be aware of effective dates and any subsequent rule changes (e.g., Jan 20, 2024 and Sep. 5, 2023 notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of USPTO Trademark Verified USPTO.gov Account Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a verified USPTO.gov account requires compliance with the USPTO Trademark Verified USPTO.gov Account Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement (available at USPTO site) contains specific sponsorship obligations; attorneys are expected to read and follow the Agreement's terms when sponsoring support staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Sponsorship Tool is the sole sponsorship method
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Trademark Sponsorship Tool is, and has been, the sole method for an attorney to sponsor the USPTO.gov accounts of trademark support staff from the attorney's USPTO.gov account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys must use the Trademark Sponsorship Tool (see USPTO guide) to sponsor accounts; other methods do not satisfy the formal sponsorship process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney certification when sponsoring via the Trademark Sponsorship Tool
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the Trademark Sponsorship Tool, the attorney must certify on-screen that (a) they grant access to the listed individual(s) to work under the sponsoring attorney's direction and control; (b) they are responsible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.18 for actions taken under the attorney's authority by the sponsored individual(s); and (c) they have read and understand the Terms of Use and all applicable USPTO customer account agreements and agree to abide by them and USPTO rules and policies regarding customer accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The on-screen checkbox is an explicit acknowledgment of responsibilities and potential liability under USPTO professional conduct rules; attorneys should not check it unless they will supervise and accept responsibility for sponsored users' activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor only directly employed/retained and supervised support staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring attorney may only sponsor support staff who (a) are directly employed or retained by the attorney, the attorney's company, or the attorney's law firm and (b) work under the attorney's direct supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring family members or individuals who are not employed/retained and directly supervised is improper and violates the Verified Account Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sponsor foreign or domestic company/group/client/agent/other practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring attorneys must not attempt to sponsor any foreign or domestic company, group, client, agent, attorney or other practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Verified Account Agreement expressly prohibits sponsorship of entities or persons that are not attorney support staff; such sponsorships risk misuse and disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each support staff must have separate USPTO.gov account (no sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each attorney support staff sponsored must have a separate trademark verified USPTO.gov account in their own name; accounts are not permitted to be shared among support staff individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts are intended for individual use; shared accounts undermine identity verification and can facilitate unauthorized filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney responsibility for conduct of sponsored support staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The sponsoring attorney is responsible for the conduct of each attorney support staff acting under the sponsoring attorney's supervision when using a sponsored USPTO.gov account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility includes actions taken under the attorney's authority and may give rise to discipline under professional conduct rules (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure sponsored staff are familiar with agreement, laws, regulations, policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring attorneys must take reasonable steps to ensure that each sponsored attorney support staff is familiar with the terms of the USPTO Trademark Verified Account Agreement and with the relevant laws, regulations, and policies of the USPTO with respect to the duties to which their access pertains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable steps may include training, written instructions, and documentation that sponsored staff understand account use limitations and submission responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure sponsored staff access/use consistent with assigned tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring attorneys must take reasonable steps to ensure that each sponsored attorney support staff's access and use of USPTO systems is consistent with the tasks assigned to that individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit privileges and monitor activity so that sponsored accounts are not used beyond the individual's job responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt removal of sponsorship when support staff no longer supervised
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring attorneys must promptly remove the sponsorship of the USPTO.gov account where the attorney support staff is no longer under the attorney's employ and/or supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to promptly remove sponsorship creates risk of unauthorized filings and potential discipline; implement offboarding procedures to remove sponsorships immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate removal and reporting when misuse or abuse suspected
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring attorneys must immediately remove sponsorship of the USPTO.gov account for any attorney support staff whom the sponsoring attorney has reason to believe has abused or misused any USPTO system (including knowingly submitting false statements or signatures), and immediately report the misuse or abuse to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected abuse promptly (e.g., TMScams or other USPTO channels) and preserve evidence; immediate removal is required under the Verified Account Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and follow USPTO Trademark Rules of Practice and TMEP guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners assisting clients in trademark matters before the Office should know the rules governing practice before the Office, including the guidance set forth in the Trademark Manual of Examining Procedure (TMEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with TMEP and USPTO trademark practice rules is an expectation of competent practice and helps prevent violations that may harm clients or the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide competent representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must provide competent representation to clients; failing to review relevant account agreements or sponsoring prohibited persons can violate this standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence includes understanding and complying with the Verified Account Agreement and Terms of Use before sponsoring accounts; lack of such review was cited as a § 11.101 violation in this matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conduct prejudicial to USPTO administration (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners shall not engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of the USPTO trademark registration system; violating account sponsorship rules (e.g., sponsoring prohibited persons) may constitute such conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper sponsorship undermines the integrity of the trademark register and may be disciplined as prejudicial conduct under §11.804(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor for unauthorized filings and report suspected fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners who sponsor USPTO.gov accounts should regularly and frequently search the USPTO's online trademark search system for applications naming them as the current attorney of record for applications filed over a given period, using search phrases such as 'AT: firstname AND AT: lastname AND FD: (YYYYMMDD TO YYYYMMDD)' and compare results to the attorney's list of actual application filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unauthorized filings are found, the attorney should promptly inform the USPTO via TMScams@uspto.gov. Regular monitoring is a recommended mitigation practice to detect misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary consequences and publication of sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of the account sponsorship rules and applicable USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct can lead to disciplinary sanctions such as public reprimand, electronic publication of the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room, and publication of a notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may be publicly posted and prior disciplinary records may be considered in future proceedings as aggravating factors. Respondents may be required to waive reconsideration/appeal as part of settlement agreements.
